post.title: Marble Skill Taxonomy
post.hook: 1,590 things a child learns, wired together by 3,221 prerequisite edges.
post.summary: An open dataset that breaks primary and elementary learning into micro-topics, links them in a prerequisite graph, and aligns them to national curriculum standards. It was released as v1 on 2026-07-08 with validators and an explorer app.
post.writeup:
## What it is
The Marble Skill Taxonomy is an open, structured map of what children learn in the primary and elementary years. It holds 1,590 micro-topics across 8 subjects, joined by 3,221 prerequisite dependencies, and aligned to 7 curricula with 3,261 standards.

## Why it was made
Most curriculum data is either a flat list of standards or locked inside a product. This release treats learning as a connected graph, so you can ask what a learner must master before a given idea.

## How it works
Each topic is a single teachable idea with a plain-language description, mastery evidence, a type (conceptual, procedural, representational, language or meta), a subject, a domain and an age range. Each dependency says topic X depends on prerequisite Y, is tagged hard or soft, and carries a one-line reason. 183 domain clusters give parent-friendly summaries per subject, domain and age band.

The repo ships plain JSON, JSON Schemas, a dependency-free validator that checks referential integrity and SHA-256 checksums, and a React and Vite explorer.

## Findings
Science (547) and Mathematics (503) make up most of the topics, followed by English at 286. Of the 3,221 edges, 2,025 are hard and 1,196 are soft. Standards for the UK National Curriculum and Common Core ship with full text. NGSS, C3 and IB PYP ship as codes only, because Marble cannot relicense them.

## Licensing
The database is ODbL 1.0, the authored text is CC BY-SA 4.0, and the standards keep their upstream licenses.

## Open questions
Full text for the codes-only sources depends on rights clearance. Embeddings are excluded from this release, and so is all per-child data.
